exact_original_alert.finding: Published thm-laurent-coefficient-formula-and-uniqueness, proof step 2.1, says “therefore every finite sum equals” 2πi c_n. The truncated sum ranges over −N≤k≤N, so this equality requires N≥|n|. For example, f(z)=z, a=0, n=1 and N=0 give zero for the truncated integral although c_1=1. The eventual equality suffices for the limit argument; the word “every” lacks this index qualification.

mathematical_disposition: For fixed n, monomial integration vanishes unless k=n. The truncated integral is zero if N<|n| and equals2pi i c_n once N>=|n|. Thus the sequence of integrals is eventually constant and has the claimed limit. Uniform convergence on the circle is part of the supplied convergent-Laurent definition, and multiplication by the fixed bounded circle weight preserves it. The proof applies to positive and negative n and every interior radius, including punctured/exterior annuli; coefficient uniqueness follows from the unchanged formula.
